Why it matters: Surprise wins across the map for Democrats — including in the Deep South — complicate a lot for the Trump administration. Republicans have relied on a simple-majority funding mechanism known as reconciliation to pay for marquee projects like Golden Dome . That option is now a long shot over the next few months, and impossible after that. Outrage over the Iran war, well beyond the half-year mark, is sure to turbocharge a long list of congressional inquiries. And lawmakers on both sides of the aisle, including Reps. Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.) and Thomas Massie (R-Ky.), have suggested impeaching Hegseth. Follow the money: Defense analysts agree prospects for the administration's full $1.5 trillion defense budget look grim.

items.title: Molecular imaging reveals how shape-shifting protein complex captures DNA and holds separate sections together
items.summary: Researchers at Kanazawa University and the National Institute of Genetics in Japan have used high-speed atomic force microscopy to observe how a group of proteins known as Smc5/6 interacts with DNA. The images reveal how this structure opens and closes, captures DNA and brings separate sections together. The researchers also observed Smc5/6 holding twisted sections of DNA in place, producing more tightly packed arrangements. The findings, published in Nature Communications, provide new insights into the molecular processes that contribute to the maintenance and repair of genetic material.

Wild animals can now GPS-collar themselves for research
items.summary: For six decades, wildlife researchers have faced a persistent challenge: to attach a tracking device to study a wild animal, they first have to catch it. Now, a new approach developed at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU) allows GPS collars to be deployed autonomously on free-roaming terrestrial wildlife. Published in BioScience, the proof-of-concept study demonstrates Capture-Free Telemetry (CFT), a technique that places tracking devices on wild animals as they interact with baited deployment units in their natural habitat.

ROME (AP) — Next year’s Giro d’Italia will start in Trieste, cross briefly into Slovenia, and climb up three iconic mountains in the final week before the mostly ceremonial finish in Rome.The route for the 110th Giro, scheduled for May 8-30, was presented in Rome on Monday. The 21 stages will be made up of: two time trials, six sprint stages, eight medium mountain legs and five in the high mountains on a total route of 3,418.9 kilometers (2,124.4 miles). The Giro will open with a 172-kilometer stage that starts and finishes in Trieste, crossing the nearby border briefly into Slovenia. The second stage is entirely in Slovenia before crossing back into Italy for the rest of the race.

Dennis Gates hosts his old team, led by his former assistant, to tip off the 2026-27 campaign For much of its history, Cleveland State was a fairly run of the mill low major program. Is that water in your spacecraft, or are you just happy to see the delta-V. The brothers launched rockets, refurbished rockets, and sold rockets. But when it came time for them to leave SpaceX and start their own space company—a lifetime dream for the Carlisle brothers—they chose not to build rockets. Rather, they focused on spacecraft. In late 2022, the three Carlisles founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. They chose water, which is potentially harvestable on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, as a means of propulsion.

The 1972 Miami Dolphins celebrated this weekend after the previously-undefeated Vikings lost, but one member of the historic team passed away. According to an obituary published on Legacy, former Dolphins defensive lineman Bob Heinz died on Saturday at 79 years old. Heinz played collegiately at Delta College and the University of the Pacific before the Dolphins took him in the second round (No. 37 overall) of the 1969 NFL Draft. He spent nine seasons with Miami, appearing in 111 games and recording nine sacks. With Heinz on the roster, the Dolphins won two Super Bowls, including in 1972 when Miami became the first and only team to ever finish a full season without a loss on their record.

The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner. New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial. The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer. Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations. More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.

Illinois high school football could return to its old schedule and playoff format under new IHSA proposals. Proposal 16 is a major move submitted by Camp Point Central . It would restore "the 2025-26 football practice, contest and pre-season practice schedules/requirements including the reinstatement of the 0-week scrimmage and the Monday of week 6 first day of practice/acclimatization.
